grammar.title: Recognise a formal identification or statement
grammar.formation: Noun + でございます, a formal polite alternative to です. Existence uses ございます for ある; animate own-side presence commonly uses おります.
grammar.explanation: The caller hears a company or department name before the purpose of a call. でございます identifies it formally; it does not by itself honour a particular person. Ordinary internal conversations can use です. Distinguish identification from presence: 会議室でございます identifies the room; 会議室がございます says one exists. Earlier polite forms are retrieved here in a phone and visitor-service setting.

examples.ja: {営業|えいぎょう}{部|ぶ}でございます。
{会場|かいじょう}は{三階|さんがい}のC{室|しつ}でございます。
examples.en: The venue is Room C on the third floor.

examples.ja: {受付|うけつけ}に{資料|しりょう}がございます。

grammar.mistake: Do not mechanically add で before every ございます. Match the intended identification or existence. Historical でござる is not the default voice for a modern office.

grammar.title: Check availability before asking
grammar.formation: 恐れ入りますが + a concrete question or request. Internal availability check: 今、少しよろしいですか / 今、話してもいいですか.
grammar.explanation: 恐れ入りますが acknowledges the trouble before a request. Follow it with what you need, such as repeating a name; it is not the request by itself. A familiar internal colleague can speak more directly while remaining polite. If the person cannot talk now, agree on another time. These are useful choices rather than words required before every sentence.
grammar.example: 恐れ入りますが、もう一度お名前をお願いします。
grammar.translation: Sorry, could you give your name once more?

examples.ja: {恐|おそ}れ{入|い}りますが、もう{一度|いちど}お{名前|なまえ}をお{願|ねが}いします。
examples.en: Sorry, could you give your name once more?

examples.ja: {今|いま}、{少|すこ}しよろしいですか。
{今|いま}は{難|むずか}しいでしょうか。{後|あと}で{掛|か}け{直|なお}します。
examples.en: Is now difficult? I’ll call again later.

grammar.mistake: Do not assume that a soft opening makes an impossible deadline acceptable. Confirm the recipient has time, and keep the request clear.

grammar.title: Introduce yourself without changing whose name it is
grammar.formation: Own name + と申します. In a call, company/team + の + own name + と申します is a conventional formal introduction.
grammar.explanation: 申す is a deferential way of saying something by your own side; と申します introduces your name to the listener. It is not the respectful verb for the client introducing themself. Internal colleagues who already know each other can simply use です. Ask a client’s name with お名前を… rather than asking them to 申す. This retrieves N4 extra-modest forms in a complete phone turn.
grammar.example: 森のチームのバオと申します。

examples.ja: {森|もり}のチームのバオと{申|もう}します。
{営業|えいぎょう}{部|ぶ}の{石川|いしかわ}と{申|もう}します。
examples.en: This is Ishikawa from the sales department.

examples.ja: {私|わたし}はバオと{申|もう}します。

grammar.mistake: Do not ask a client お名前は何と申しますか. That makes the client’s act deferential; お名前を伺ってもよろしいですか is a respectful alternative.

grammar.title: Refer to your colleague from the caller’s perspective
grammar.formation: To an external client: 石川は席を外しております. Neutral identifying role is possible: 課長の石川. Internally/directly: 石川課長, 今よろしいですか.
grammar.explanation: When representing your company to a client, refer to your own-side colleague without raising them above the client. おります is a deferential own-side presence form; いらっしゃいます asks about the respected other party. A job title can identify the role without acting as an honorific suffix. Internally you still address Ishikawa respectfully. Relationship and institution matter: this company convention is not a universal ban on titles in every school, family or mixed group.
grammar.example: 石川は、ただ今席を外しております。
grammar.translation: Ishikawa is away from their desk at the moment.

examples.ja: {石川|いしかわ}は、ただ{今|いま}{席|せき}を{外|はず}しております。
examples.en: Ishikawa is away from their desk at the moment.

examples.ja: {課長|かちょう}の{石川|いしかわ}からお{電話|でんわ}します。
examples.en: Our section manager Ishikawa will call you.

examples.ja: {石川|いしかわ}{課長|かちょう}、{今|いま}よろしいですか。
examples.en: Ishikawa-kachō, is now a good time?

grammar.mistake: Do not use 石川様はいらっしゃいます to elevate your own company’s manager to a client. Do not turn this into a rule to speak disrespectfully to the manager directly.

dialogues.title: An internal call about the demonstration

readings.title: A handover memo: request versus confirmed schedule
paragraphs: {電話|でんわ}の{引|ひ}き{継|つ}ぎメモ。{田村|たむら}{様|さま}から{石川|いしかわ}{課長|かちょう}への{伝言|でんごん}です。{田村|たむら}{様|さま}は{大阪|おおさか}からお{電話|でんわ}くださいました。{課長|かちょう}は{離席|りせき}{中|ちゅう}で、{一時|いちじ}ごろに{戻|もど}る{予定|よてい}だとお{伝|つた}えしました。まだ{課長|かちょう}とは{話|はな}せていません。

{折|お}り{返|かえ}しの{電話|でんわ}は、{本日|ほんじつ}の{午後|ごご}{一時半|いちじはん}から{二時|にじ}の{間|あいだ}をご{希望|きぼう}です。{番号|ばんごう}はいつもの{連絡先|れんらくさき}でよいと{確認|かくにん}しました。{二時|にじ}を{過|す}ぎると{別|べつ}の{打|う}ち{合|あ}わせがあるため、この{時間|じかん}{帯|たい}に{話|はな}せない{場合|ばあい}は、まずメールでご{都合|つごう}を{伺|うかが}ってください。

{用件|ようけん}は{来週|らいしゅう}{火曜|かよう}の{実演|じつえん}です。{電車|でんしゃ}が{十時十分|じゅうじじゅっぷん}に{着|つ}くので、{開始|かいし}を{十時|じゅうじ}から{十時半|じゅうじはん}にできないかとのご{相談|そうだん}でした。{難|むずか}しければ{別|べつ}の{日|ひ}でもよいとのことです。{開始|かいし}{時刻|じこく}の{変更|へんこう}は、まだ{決|き}まっていません。

{課長|かちょう}には、まず{森|もり}さんとC{室|しつ}の{空|あ}き{状況|じょうきょう}をご{確認|かくにん}いただきたいです。{返答|へんとう}をいただくまで、{社内|しゃない}の{予定|よてい}{表|ひょう}は{十時|じゅうじ}のままにしてあります。{資料|しりょう}の{配付|はいふ}は{受付|うけつけ}で{行|おこな}い、{実演|じつえん}そのものは{四十五分|よんじゅうごふん}の{予定|よてい}です。{開始|かいし}{時刻|じこく}が{決|き}まったら、オンラインの{方|かた}にも{新|あたら}しい{案内|あんない}をお{送|おく}りください。バオ。

glosses.text: お電話くださいました
glosses.kana: おでんわくださいました
glosses.meaning: called us, respectfully acknowledging the caller

glosses.text: まだ課長とは話せていません
glosses.kana: まだかちょうとははなせていません
glosses.meaning: have not been able to speak to the manager yet

glosses.text: 午後一時半から二時の間
glosses.kana: ごごいちじはんからにじのあいだ
glosses.meaning: between one-thirty and two in the afternoon

glosses.kana: いつものれんらくさき
よいとかくにんしました

glosses.meaning: if you cannot speak during that time

glosses.text: ご都合を伺ってください
glosses.kana: ごつごうをうかがってください
glosses.meaning: please ask the client what timing works

glosses.text: 変更は、まだ決まっていません
glosses.kana: へんこうは、まだきまっていません
glosses.meaning: the change has not been settled yet

glosses.kana: ごかくにんいただきたい

glosses.text: 十時のままにしてあります
glosses.kana: じゅうじのままにしてあります
glosses.meaning: have deliberately kept it at ten

exercises.prompt: What duration is planned for Tuesday’s demonstration?
exercises.explain: Ishikawa says 四十五分を予定しています.

options: Online, while Ishikawa shares the screen
exercises.explain: Mori joins online; Ishikawa shares the screen.

exercises.prompt: When will Bao start setting up?
exercises.explain: Bao says 九時半から準備します; this is setup, not visitor reception.

exercises.context: Form practice: complete the formal identification of the sales department with でございます.
exercises.explain: A department name followed by でございます identifies who answers; がございます would concern existence.

exercises.context: Form practice: say that materials are available at reception, using the formal existence form.
exercises.line: {受付|うけつけ}に{資料|しりょう}＿＿。
exercises.explain: The sentence locates existing materials, not identifies someone as materials.

exercises.context: You did not catch an external caller’s name. Choose a considerate request for repetition.
exercises.line: もう{一度|いちど}{名前|なまえ}を{言|い}ってほしい。
options: {恐|おそ}れ{入|い}りますが、もう{一度|いちど}お{名前|なまえ}をお{願|ねが}いします。
{名前|なまえ}が{悪|わる}いので、{変|か}えてください。
exercises.explain: The first both softens and specifies the request. The second stops before asking; the third insults and changes the request.

exercises.meaning: Constrained form practice: address your manager, then check whether now is a good time.
exercises.explain: A brief availability check works in the internal call. This is one authored order, not the only polite wording.
Nine-thirty is staff preparation. Visitor reception explicitly begins 九時四十五分.

exercises.prompt: How does a visitor obtain the online link?
options: Reply by three the previous afternoon; the link follows the reply
Wait for a recording after the event
exercises.explain: The third paragraph specifies the reply deadline and link delivery.
The last paragraph promises a question-and-answer summary, not photos or video or a purchase.

exercises.prompt: What is known about Ishikawa’s return?
options: They will certainly return at ten-thirty
exercises.explain: The learner says 一時ごろの予定, not confirmed presence or a guarantee.

exercises.prompt: When does Tamura request a callback today?
exercises.explain: 一時半から二時の間 is the requested callback window, distinct from the next-week event.

exercises.prompt: What does Tamura request about next Tuesday?
options: Move the ten o’clock start to ten-thirty, or consider another day
exercises.explain: Tamura requests ten-thirty because the train arrives at ten-ten and offers another day if difficult.

exercises.context: Form practice: introduce YOUR OWN name to a client with the deferential verb 申す.
exercises.explain: 申します is your deferential self-introduction; the other choices do not form it.

exercises.context: Form practice: tell an external client your own colleague Ishikawa is away. Complete the own-side deferential progressive.
exercises.line: {石川|いしかわ}は{席|せき}を{外|はず}して＿＿。
exercises.explain: 席を外しております describes your own-side colleague’s temporary absence.

exercises.context: You represent your company to an external client asking for your manager Ishikawa. Choose the own-side colleague reference.
exercises.line: {石川|いしかわ}が{今|いま}{席|せき}にいない。
options: {石川|いしかわ}は、ただ{今|いま}{席|せき}を{外|はず}しております。
{石川|いしかわ}{様|さま}は、ただ{今|いま}{席|せき}を{外|はず}していらっしゃいます。
{石川|いしかわ}さん、{今|いま}よろしいですか。
exercises.explain: The first refers to your own colleague to an outsider. The second elevates your own manager over the client; the third directly addresses Ishikawa rather than answers the client.

exercises.meaning: Constrained form practice: identify Tamura’s message first, then say you will pass it on to Ishikawa.
exercises.explain: The learner will pass on a message, not confirm the requested new start.

exercises.prompt: What schedule remains recorded while the reply is pending?
exercises.explain: The last paragraph explicitly keeps the internal schedule at ten until there is a reply.

exercises.prompt: What should happen if today’s callback window cannot be used?
options: Call without checking during Tamura’s later meeting
exercises.explain: The second paragraph directs an email availability check, not an assumption that silence cancels the request.

exercises.prompt: What needs checking before agreeing to the new start?
options: Mori’s availability and Room C availability
Whether the brochure has already been printed
exercises.explain: The handover asks Ishikawa to check Mori and Room C before confirming the change.

recycling.reason: A meeting confirmation and a caller’s request use earlier schedule, reply and telephone vocabulary where it fits. Committee headwords are supplementary genre recognition; they are not stuffed into the calls to reach the default recycling percentage.

grammar: formal identification でございます
own-side reference おります and self-introduction と申します
watch.prompt: Optionally listen to a workplace call you may use. Note the requested action, current arrangement and any condition before a change is confirmed. Do not infer a decision just from a courteous acknowledgement.
